newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks creep back in black by close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks creep back in black by close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2450 +13 US 30yr cl 7.09 +0.04
10yrbond futs 92.160 +0.045 Gold NY 342.95 Lon fix 342.20
*Stocks crawl back into black by close, trade thin as wages data absorbed, inflation now focus. Volume 312.51 million, value A$566.07 million, 1,040 stocks traded, 295 steady, 376 up, 369 down.

A lightly-traded Australian share market eked out wafer thin gains by the close on Tuesday as traders digested a wages verdict from the the Australian Industrial Relations Commission that was largely in line with market expectations.
Nervous eyes now turned to Wednesday's March quarter inflation figures as players attempted to divine the Reserve Bank of Australia's monetary policy intentions.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index added 1.8 points to 2,447.6. June share price index futures ended 13 points higher at 2,450, a 2.4 point premium to the index.
"It was very quiet yesterday and that has continued on today," said David Iron, head of institutional sales at HSBC James Capel.
"The wage outcome was well-received. One positive is that people are now accepting we are in a low inflation environment."
From here attention turned to the consumer price index data due on Wednesday, with stronger turnover expected once the numbers were out of the way.
"People hate uncertainty, so there will probably be better activity tomorrow once the figures are out of the way," said a Melbourne-based dealer.
Despite the slow overall trade, individual features popped up in both sectors.

In the resources, oil and gas major Woodside Petroleum jumped to a record high of A$10.07 before easing to close 11 cents higher at A$10.00 after the Monday's formal approval of funding for the Laminaria/Corallina venture.

Gold/nickel miner Resolute jumped 13 cents to an intraday high of A$2.75 before easing back to square at A$2.62 after it announced it had finalised a A$120 million funding package for its Bulong nickel project in Western Australia.
Major miner WMC slumped in the afternoon session, closing nearly two percent lower at A$7.67, after what brokers said was a disappointing third quarter production report.

In the industrials, much-rumoured takeover target, upmarket apparel and homewares retailer Country Road, saw heavy turnover with 7.9 million shares traded, the bulk of it in three lines specialled through J.B. Were. Brokers speculated that offshore interests were perhaps between the heavy trade.
Metals recycler Simsmetal climbed to a record high A$8.24 as investors took a shine to its third quarter profit, up on the second quarter. It closed up 27.9 cents at A$8.229.
Rises barely shaded falls by the end, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures and options trade was moderately active. Total options traded 37,996. Turnover in June SPI contracts totalled 5,697.

In other local markets, short Australian bond and bill futures ended sharply higher in the aftermath of the Australian Industrial Relations Commission granting a A$10 per week pay award, which was at the lower end of expectations.
By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.82 percent, down from Monday's 7.87 percent.
The Australian dollar faltered Tuesday as the market mulled over the mixed implications of an inflation-friendly minimum wage award.
By 5.05 p.m. (0700 GMT) the local dollar had faded to US$0.7755/60 from US$0.7785/90 just before the wage news broke, but was not that far from Monday's late US$0.7765/70.
